solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One way the Germans drive out a crazy husband, covered by veto

indicators.note: crazy tells us the letters of 'out a' are jumbled into a new order
covered by means the husband letter sits inside the word for veto

parts.note: a veto is a ban on something

explanation.surface: A German motorist takes a mad husband out, under some kind of prohibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' and 'covered by' are the indicators; the definition is the German word for a motorway, literally 'car track'.
explanation.definitionFit: German motorways, the famous roads Germans drive on, carry this name.

clue.text: The Spanish force maiden into a British academy

indicators.note: into says the maiden letter goes inside the academy phrase

parts.note: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A Spanish girl is admitted to a British drama school.
explanation.walkthrough: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, London's drama school; M for maiden comes from cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: The fleet Spain sent against England in 1588 is the classic example of this naval force.

clue.text: They secure government revenue for auditors

indicators.note: auditors are listeners, so the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: tax is the revenue a government collects

explanation.surface: Government income measures for the people who audit accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditors' looks like accountants checking tax, but it just means listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: Small sharp nails, used to fix things in place, are things that secure.

clue.text: Curious university foible that avoids putting fossils into power

definitions.text: that avoids putting fossils into power

indicators.note: curious here means odd or strange, telling us to rearrange the letters

explanation.surface: An odd academic quirk that steers clear of fossil fuels in energy generation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curious' rearranges U plus FOIBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuel made from plant or animal matter replaces coal and oil, so no fossil material is burned for energy.

clue.text: Boro' making big strides towards success?

definitions.text: Boro' making big strides towards success?

parts.words: Boro' making big strides towards success?
parts.note: Boro' is the first half of Borodino, Napoleon's great battle of 1812, while the phrase also means a large part of the way to winning

explanation.surface: A football club called Boro' (Middlesbrough) is making big progress up the table.
explanation.walkthrough: Boro' looks like Middlesbrough FC's nickname; it is the first four letters of BORODINO, the 1812 battle. The second reading is the idiom for a major step towards success.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes doing the hardest part of a task, which brings you most of the way to success.

clue.text: He is entitled to hop on board?

definitions.meaning: someone with the title Sir, given by the monarch
the chess piece that jumps over others on the chessboard

explanation.surface: Someone claims the right to jump aboard a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A man honoured with the title Sir is one; so is the chess piece that leaps across the board.

clue.text: Unfortunately Jones died in operation

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of Jones are scrambled

parts.note: OB is short for obiit, Latin for 'he or she died', seen on gravestones

explanation.surface: Sadly, Mr Jones died during surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunately' signals the rearrangement; the obiit abbreviation is a gravestone convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinoplasty, cosmetic surgery to reshape the nose, is a common surgical procedure.

clue.text: Make rough opening: the moon's rising within

indicators.note: within puts the reversed moon word inside the opening word

parts.note: a grate is a grating over an opening

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Luna is the Latin name for the moon

explanation.surface: Roughen up an opening while the moon comes up inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' works upwards because this is a down clue; 'within' places the result inside a grating.
explanation.definitionFit: To form a surface into small grains gives it a rough, gritty texture.

clue.text: Lament number finally lacking teacher put back a year

indicators.note: finally lacking says the number word loses its last letter

parts.note: three is a number

indicators.note: put back means the teacher word is written in reverse

parts.note: a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A sad song whose number's ending lacks a teacher, postponed a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally lacking' trims THREE to THRE; 'put back' reverses DON to NOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A song or poem of mourning for the dead is a dirge or elegy.

clue.text: Rodents almost steal from some wood a set of little posts

indicators.note: almost says the rodents word loses its final letter

parts.note: mice are rodents
to rob is to steal from
a log is a piece of wood

explanation.surface: Mice stealing timber pieces, as if some forest rodent were thieving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims MICE to MIC. 'little posts' sounds like fence posts, but means short online messages.
explanation.definitionFit: A site of short online entries, like Twitter, is a collection of brief posted messages.

clue.text: Hand-waving from legion Tacitus misinterpreted

indicators.note: misinterpreted means read wrongly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Roman historian Tacitus misread the arm signals of a Roman legion.
explanation.walkthrough: Tacitus was a Roman historian, fitting the legion; 'misinterpreted' rearranges all thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Waving the hands and arms while speaking is making expressive movements.

clue.text: Consternation about a section of flight

indicators.note: about means the commotion word surrounds the letter A

parts.note: a stir is a commotion or state of agitation

explanation.surface: Panic over part of an air journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests aircraft, but here it is a flight of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of steps is made up of single steps, each one part of it.

clue.text: Amid signs of slack housework, one's grand contempt

indicators.note: amid places the following letters in the middle of the housework word

parts.note: dust gathering shows that the cleaning has been neglected
one is I, so one's is I'S
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: Someone sniffs at a grubby house, showing grand disdain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand' looks like an adjective for the contempt, but it is the slang for a thousand pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong revulsion or loathing is close to scorn for something.

clue.text: Stay a while; as a result, trip is by no means finished

parts.note: so means therefore or as a result

indicators.note: by no means finished says the trip word is cut short at its end

parts.note: a journey is a trip

explanation.surface: Linger a little, since the trip is far from over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by no means finished' cuts JOURNEY to JOURN.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere temporarily is to stop over for a short time.

clue.text: Here notices how pig was wounded and died

parts.note: the wild pig was shot, leaving a bullet in the boar

explanation.surface: Notices report how a pig was shot and died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Here notices' means the place where notices are pinned.
explanation.definitionFit: A noticeboard is where announcements are pinned up for people to read.

clue.text: One piece in small snack between two

indicators.note: in places the piece and the one inside the snack word

parts.note: a bite is a small snack
a part is a piece
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A single piece in a small snack shared between two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between two' looks like part of the snack scene, but it is the definition: having two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Shared by or involving two parties, as in an agreement made by two sides.

clue.text: Pro engaged in a piece of satire to invite trouble

indicators.note: engaged in places the pro word inside the satire phrase

parts.note: a skit is a short satirical sketch
for means in favour of, as pro does

explanation.surface: A professional performer in a satirical sketch invites trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pro' looks like a professional, but here it means in favour of.
explanation.definitionFit: To provoke or court bad consequences by your own behaviour is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Twice as true, power make you concentrate more?

indicators.note: make you suggests the letters are formed into something new, so they are rearranged
twice means the words 'as true' are taken two times

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Twice as true, power can force you to focus harder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twice' doubles AS TRUE; 'make you' rearranges those twelve letters with P.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemists dissolve extra solute beyond saturation point, making a solution even stronger.

clue.text: Start to repair each split, having hit a vehicle

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of repair is used

parts.note: to rend is to tear apart or split

explanation.surface: Get repairs started on each crack after a car crash.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb means to drive into the back of another car.
explanation.definitionFit: To crash into the back of a car in front is a common kind of collision.

clue.text: A way to catch old king in raid

indicators.note: to catch means the way phrase surrounds the king

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
Saul was the first king of Israel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A route used to capture an ancient king in a raid.
explanation.walkthrough: The old king is the first king of Israel in the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent attack or onslaught on a place is a raid.

clue.text: Worry over monarch's progress

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts the worry word on top of the monarch

parts.note: care is worry or anxiety
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Anxiety about how the monarch is getting on.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's course through working life, their advance in a profession, is that progress.

clue.text: Insect in tree intended heading off

parts.note: a fir is a tree

indicators.note: heading off removes the first letter of the intended word

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: An insect inside a tree, meaning to head away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' trims MEANT to EANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A stinging tropical species of ant is one kind of insect.

clue.text: A light ship heading back for old kingdom

parts.note: SS is steamship

indicators.note: heading back tells us to read the light word backwards

parts.note: airy means light, as an airy room is

explanation.surface: A light vessel turns back towards an ancient realm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading back' reverses AIRY to YRIA. 'light ship' looks like one thing; light is AIRY.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Mesopotamian empire based at Nineveh was a kingdom of the past.

clue.text: Stop working, computer finally failing, and to restore connection

indicators.note: failing says the chosen letter is missing from the stop working word

parts.note: to retire is to stop working

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word computer

explanation.surface: Retire when the computer finally dies, and reconnect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' removes R, computer's last letter, from RETIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tying something again joins it back up, as a knot re-fastens a broken link.

clue.text: Erect, beams to audience

indicators.note: to an audience means as heard, so the word is spoken

parts.note: rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: A stage lighting rig is put up and shines beams at the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erect' is a verb here: put up.
explanation.definitionFit: To build or put up a structure is to lift it up.

clue.text: Courtesy in middle of missive is quite extraordinary

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the ordinary, so the letters of quite are rearranged
middle of keeps only the inner letters of the missive word, dropping its ends

parts.note: a letter is a missive

explanation.surface: Politeness in the middle of a letter is quite remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' turns QUITE into ETIQU; 'middle of' trims LETTER to ETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: The code of polite behaviour in society is good manners.

clue.text: Like a country gentleman, initially thin and weak

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of thin

parts.note: weedy means weak and puny

explanation.surface: A country squire, thin and feeble to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: Tweed is the woollen cloth associated with British country gentry.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressed in rough woollen suits of tweed, the English squire's typical look.

clue.text: Cast-off clothing

parts.note: cast off is the knitting term for finishing the last row, so these garments are finished by casting off rather than being discarded

explanation.surface: Second-hand clothes thrown away by others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast-off' suggests hand-me-downs; it is the knitter's term for finishing a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumpers and cardigans made with needles and yarn are casted off when complete.
